items.title: Georg Brunis Interview, 1958-06-03
items.q: Vandu would pop a string, or somebody would talk, or forget or say something, we'd have to keep making it over.

ctx.x: Since they made those things. You've made those down in Richmond, Indiana. Yeah. How long did you stay on that trip? Is that a day or two? Two or three days, I think. It took Ted Lewis with Jimmy Dorsi on the clarinet to make Ann Hague's children blues. We made it from 10 o'clock in the morning, 6 o'clock in the night, and we just finished it.

Really? Oh, yeah. Every time we'd get going good, something would happen. Yeah. Vandu would pop a string, or somebody would talk, or forget or say something, we'd have to keep making it over. Yeah. That was a fabulous guy, that Lewis. Yeah.
